claims.text: Three NDA allies—LJP(RV), RLM, and TDP—urged the Election Commission of India to clarify its position on the controversy surrounding the electoral process and the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

LJP(RV) chief and Union Minister Chirag Paswan stated that it is the Election Commission's responsibility, especially Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, to firmly present its side to dispel public doubts.
RLM president Upendra Kushwaha called on the Election Commission to immediately clarify the situation regarding the special intensive revision of electoral rolls to address public confusion.
Media reports in The Indian Express revealed that two top election commissioners had raised objections multiple times to decisions made without their knowledge or consent.
In response to reports of internal differences, the Election Commission stated that differing views among members are normal and that its final decisions were unanimous.
TDP parliamentary party leader Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu stated that providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will strengthen public confidence in the Election Commission.
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray called for the complete cancellation of the recent Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process on September 25, 2026.
Raj Thackeray described the Special Intensive Revision process as a new weapon in the hands of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray stated that re-elections should be held in some states due to allegations of anomalies in voters' lists.
The Indian National Congress staged nationwide protests on September 25, 2026, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Amid the ongoing political row, the West Bengal BJP chief stated that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar deserves the Padma Bhushan award for conducting the Special Intensive Revision process.
Student leaders and activists were detained during a protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The Cockroach Janta Party threatened to launch a nationwide protest if Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar does not resign within 48 hours.

Under the 2023 Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Appointment Act, the selection committee for poll panel members consists of the prime minister, a Union Cabinet minister, and the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

Supreme Court Justice Satish Chandra Sharma disagreed with Justice Dipankar Datta on a bench hearing petitions against the 2023 Election Commissioner appointment law, after Justice Datta stated the law did not appear to ensure an independent selection process.
Justice Satish Chandra Sharma's son, Siddharth Sharma, serves as the standing counsel for the Election Commission of India in Madhya Pradesh.

Justice Satish Chandra Sharma headed a Supreme Court bench that overturned an order directing Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam to pay compensation to a detained graduate; Roopam is the daughter of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
India's youth-led Cockroach Janta Party joined opposition calls demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
